etymologies.etymologyHTML: Learned borrowing from Latin haesitatus, past participle of haesitare, intensive of haerere (“to hesitate, stick fast; to hang or hold fast”). Displaced native Old English wandian.

definitions.definition: (intransitive) To stop or pause respecting decision or action; to be in suspense or uncertainty as to a determination.

quote.citation: September 1, 1742, Alexander Pope, letter to Racine
quote.text: I shall not hesitate to declare myself very cordially, in regard to some particulars about which you have desired an answer.

definitions.definition: (intransitive) To stammer; to falter in speaking.
(transitive, poetic, rare) To utter with hesitation or to intimate by a reluctant manner.

quote.citation: a. 1724, Alexander Pope, The Ms. at Longleat:
quote.text: Just hint a fault, and hesitate dislike.
